articles.title: Como 4-1 Man Utd: Michael Carrick's side ripped apart in Italy during Champions League hammering
articles.summary: Match report as Nico Paz stars for Cesc Fabregas' Como as they take apart Manchester United; Michael Carrick's side now winless in seven games across all competitions after suffering Champions League humbling in Italy
articles.body:
The pressure continues to pile on Carrick and this United side as their start to the season lurches from bad to worse - and on Wednesday night they were humbled by a Como team that delivered more intensity and quality in Italy.

The first attribute should be a non-negotiable but, despite United's application being in the spotlight, they were once again outworked by their opposition. Static in midfield, allowing Como players to run off them, losing markers... this was a shocking show of United's big failings out of possession.

The tone was set just two minutes in when Man Utd went behind early on - again. They are the first English side to concede in back-to-back Champions League games so soon and never got to grips with Cesc Fabregas' impressively coached team.

Nico Paz brought the class for the hosts. The talented Argentina international stuck the opener into the top corner when Harry Maguire gave him too much space and then slotted in a third after catching Carlos Baleba in possession.

Paz set up another Como goal, too, playing in Tasos Douvikas, who ran away from a disoriented Matthijs de Ligt to find the net inside four minutes of the second half.

This was De Ligt's first start in 325 days due to back problems and came due to a wider spate of injuries at the club. But excuses for this United performance may wear thin quickly for the travelling support who stood in the pouring rain to watch this dismantling.

United's own star, Bruno Fernandes, was anonymous again, with just one goal involvement now in his past nine appearances for the club. His head-shaking summed up the mood before a sweeping Como fourth, which saw unmarked centre-back Jacobo Ramon head in, underlining the vast gap between the sides on the night.

Joshua Zirkzee's injury-time goal was of little consolation. With just three points from their first three games, United have an uphill battle to make it out of the league phase in this competition. More immediately they are in desperate need of a better performance and win at home to Bournemouth on Sunday in the Premier League, live on Sky Sports.

Carrick 'really angry' with Man Utd performance

Manchester United boss Michael Carrick :

"I'm really angry but you've got to move on and deal with what's next. At this moment in time, there's a lot to do before the next game to get the team ready, because that was a difficult night for everybody.

"It's not about playing for me - it's about playing for this club. My whole life's wrapped around it [Man Utd]. I genuinely give everything I possibly can. It's not about me, it's about what we all give."

Asked if all of the players give as much as he does, Carrick said: "I'd like to think so. I didn't like what I saw tonight though."

Analysis: No shock to see Man Utd beaten

"They've got to start winning matches. The problem with Manchester United is we still live in the age of when it was [Wayne] Rooney, [Cristiano] Ronaldo and people like that.

"We're caught by the name - one of the biggest clubs in the world. But they're not one of the biggest teams in the world. They're far from it. Everybody judges them on when they had superstars.

"I don't see it as a shock. I look at their players and I don't go, 'oh this is a surprise'. I didn't expect them to beat Leeds. Absolutely not. I didn't expect them to beat Como. That's where they are.

"Rooney, Ronaldo, [Roy] Keane... they're a million miles away."

'Como defeat is one of Man Utd's worst ever in Europe'

'One of Man Utd's worst ever defeats in Europe'

"Michael Carrick looked very angry. He's the first one to defend his players whenever he can.

"It was one of those games where you know from the first minutes that United weren't at it. The body language from some of those players... you could tell Carrick was frustrated.

"Let's not sugar coat it - this is one of their worst ever results in Europe.

"This was a pretty surprising and shocking performance, but I think it's been coming as well. My feeling is that watching this game has told us what we've been thinking about this Manchester United team.

"There will be speculation about how that changing room is feeling and whether Michael Carrick still has them on board. But tonight, it doesn't quite feel everyone is on board.

"Ultimately there's a lot more pressure on Carrick and his position at Manchester United."

Manchester United are winless in seven consecutive games in all competitions (D3 L4) for the first time since a run of eight matches between November and December 2015.

Manchester United are the first English team to concede inside the opening two minutes of back-to-back major European games (47 seconds vs Atletico Madrid, 118 seconds vs Como).

Como completed 594 passes tonight, the most by a team in a Champions League game against Manchester United since Barcelona in April 2019 (725).

2: BIG MISS! Diogo Dalot takes a Matheus Cunha cross down in the box but his left-foot shot flashes wide of the far post.

2: GOAL! Nico Paz curls Como's opener into the top corner after Harry Maguire gives him too much space. A similar chance to Dalot's - a different result!

17: WIDE! Harry Maguire heads wide from a Bryan Mbeumo cross.

39: BIG MISS! Tasos Douvikas blazes over after stepping into the United box, failing to capitalise on static defending.

41: OFFIDE! A let-off for Senne Lammens and Man Utd as an offside flag goes up against Douvikas after he is brought down in the box by the goalkeeper.

HT: SUBS! Michael Carrick makes two changes at the break with Amad Diallo and Carlos Baleba sent on for Andrey Santos and Matheus Cunha.

49: GOAL! Man Utd concede at the start of the second half, too, as Paz plays in Douvikas, who runs off Matthijs de Ligt before firing in.

54: CLOSE! Lucas da Cunha blasts a left-foot shot wide from inside the box when he looked primed to add a third.

57: GOAL! Baleba makes an ill-advised turn in his own half with no cover behind him and Paz takes the ball and races in on goal to add a third.

64: CHANCES! But Amad can't connect with Fernandes' clipped pass into the box to pull one back for United. Moments later he sees a shot tipped over.

76: GOAL! Centre-back Jacobo Ramon heads in to finish off another sweeping Como move.

articles.title: El Asisa Joventut sufre para ganar (76-74), pero ya es líder en solitario
articles.standfirst: Los verdinegros se apoyan en Sulejmanovic (17 puntos) y Laprovittola (16) para doblegar a un Telekom Bonn que falló un triple para ganar
articles.summary: Los verdinegros se apoyan en Sulejmanovic (17 puntos) y Laprovittola (16) para doblegar a un Telekom Bonn que falló un triple para ganar
articles.body: El Asisa Joventut sufrió este miércoles hasta el final para ganar al Telekom Bonn alemán por 76-74 y se colocó como líder en solitario del grupo H de la Liga de Campeones de la FIBA. Emir Sulejmanovic y Nico Laprovittola, con 33 puntos entre ambos, fueron piezas fundamentales para que los verdinegros lograran el triunfo ante un Bonn que tuvo el tiro sobre la bocina para ganar, pero Joel Aminu falló. El partido comenzó de la peor de las maneras para el Asisa Joventut, con la lesión del base sueco Ludde Hakanson, que sufrió una torcedura importante de tobillo y no volvió a jugar más en todo el encuentro. Poco después, el ala-pívot estadounidense Kwan Cheatham sufrió un golpe fuerte en un dedo, que tuvieron que recolocarle, y minutos después ya pudo volver a jugar. En los primeros minutos, fue Eli Ndiaye el jugador más destacado de los catalanes para poner la primera ventaja en el marcador (14-10, min. 7). Sin embargo, los alemanes fueron a más en ataque y lograron darle la vuelta para llegar al final del primer cuarto con un resultado de 19-22 en un ambiente algo frío en Badalona. La buena dinámica del Telekom Bonn siguió en el segundo cuarto gracias a la inspiración de Marcus Foster, que en pocos minutos tuvo un porcentaje superior al 70 %, aspecto que hizo que los suyos tuvieran su primera gran ventaja (23-28, min. 12). Sin embargo, cuando mejor estuvieron los visitantes en pista, en la Penya volvió a aparecer Ndiaye para volver a igualar el encuentro, aunque aún no fue suficiente para empezar a dominar en el marcador (33-35, min. 18). Los últimos minutos de primera mitad se convirtieron en un intercambio de canastas que, como era de esperar, benefició al equipo que ya estaba por delante, y el Telekom Bonn se marchó al descanso con un 36-40 frente a un Asisa Joventut que no mostró ni mucho menos su mejor versión. En la reanudación, pese a que los alemanes siguieron con acierto, el Asisa Joventut mejoró en ambos lados de la pista, y la buena mano de Álex Reyes hizo que el partido se mantuviera con igualdad (43-44, min. 25). Aunque si alguien puso el equipo a sus espaldas fue el ala-pívot Emir Sulejmanovic, que fue pieza clave en el rebote ofensivo para anotar segundas oportunidades y poner por delante a su equipo después de mucho tiempo (50-49, min. 28). A diferencia de los cuartos anteriores, los de Dani Miret consiguieron acabar el tercer periodo por delante (55-54), un aspecto que, sin embargo, no hizo bajar el nivel del Telekom Bonn en el inicio de los últimos diez minutos de partido. En el último cuarto, los alemanes volvieron a ponerse por delante, pero cuando más quemó el balón apareció la figura de Nico Laprovittola para que los suyos volvieran a dominar y poner en pie al público presente en el Olímpic (65-60, min. 35). El jugador argentino fue a más, y otros cuatro puntos prácticamente seguidos suyos pusieron tierra de por medio para que el Asisa Joventut estuviera a punto de lograr la victoria (69-63, min. 38). Al final, el Asisa Joventut venció por 76-74 al Telekom Bonn para ponerse como líder en solitario e invicto del grupo H, justo antes de su primer desplazamiento en la competición la próxima jornada a Oporto. 76 - Asisa Joventut (19+17+19+21): Hakanson (-), Laprovittola (16), Torres (3), Ndiaye (8), Sulejmanovic (17) -cinco inicial-; Rubio (5), Reyes (5), Nogués (4), Niebla (2), Birgander (4) y Cheatham (12). 74 - Telekom Bonn (22+18+14+20): Foster (14), Aminu (13), Garrett (17), Murphy (8), Kessens (-) -cinco inicial-; Wright (8), Comithier (4), Kovacevic (2), Jostmann (6) y Kratzer (2). Árbitros: Ademir Zurapovic, Lorenzo Baldini y Edgard Ceccarelli. Sin eliminados. Incidencias: Partido correspondiente a la segunda jornada de la fase regular de la Liga de Campeones de baloncesto disputado en el Palau Municipal d'Esports de Badalona.

articles.title: Bruguémanía
articles.standfirst: El jugador catalán del Levante consigue su segundo doblete en Primera División
articles.summary: El jugador catalán del Levante consigue su segundo doblete en Primera División
articles.body: A Brugué también le daban dos, como citaba el pretérito anuncio de los yogures, aunque en este caso el jugador catalán del Levante, los reparte. Ya lo hizo hace dos meses ante el Real Betis y este miércoles, en el partido ante el Athletic Club correspondiente de la jornada 6 de Primera División, lo ha vuelto hacer. El atacante catalán consiguió perforar hasta en dos ocasiones la meta de Unai Simón, en el importante triunfo del equipo del barrio de Orriols que da oxígeno y distancia, para alcanzar la permanencia en la máxima categoría del fútbol español y evitar la zona roja de la tabla clasificatoria. Sin haber disparado entre los tres palos, el “siete” granota aprovechó en rechace dentro del área para que, sin pensárselo, fusilar con un zurdazo la portería visitante. Un minuto más tarde, con la euforia del primer gol de la tarde, anotó el segundo. Y prácticamente, con la misma dinámica. Tras una pérdida del equipo vasco dentro de la zona, Iván Romero asistió a Thiago y, tras una primera parada de Unai, el esférico le cayó al jugador catalán para hacer el segundo del encuentro. Con este doblete, Roger Brugué se coloca como máximo anotador del Levante en esta temporada, con un total de cinco goles registrados. Seguido por Iván Romero, otro de los delanteros del equipo, con tres tantos. Otro de los jugadores que han dejaron huella sobre el verde fue Etta Eyong. El delantero camerunés, que regresó a los terrenos de juego tras un mes apartado por una lesión muscular, consiguió el definitivo tercer tanto de la victoria granota ante el equipo de San Mamés.

articles.title: Camina hacia la historia
articles.standfirst: Un gol de Isco de penalti tumba al Feyenoord y deja al Betis muy cerca de la siguiente fase
articles.summary: Un gol de Isco de penalti tumba al Feyenoord y deja al Betis muy cerca de la siguiente fase
articles.body: Han tenido que pasar 21 años para que el Betis vuelve a codearse con los grandes de Europa. Y ya que ha esperado tanto, ha decidido que el regreso debía ser a lo grande. Hasta el punto de que, con solo tres jornadas disputadas, tiene pie y medio en la siguiente fase. La victoria ante el Feyenoord, gracias al gol de penalti de Isco, está a punto de lograr una clasificación sin precedentes en su historia. Así de bestia. Como suena. Por situarlo en contexto. El Benfica, con nueve puntos fue el que sacó el último billete en la pasada edición, la 25-26, para acceder a la eliminatoria de dieciséisavos. Después de ocho partidos. El Betis, con tres, ya los tiene. Y en su única participación en Champions, en la 05-06, el equipo no pudo pasar de la fase de grupos. La historia asoma a la vuelta de la esquina. Y es historia buscada, merecida. Porque el Betis fue a por el Lille en Francia, sometió al Oporto en La Cartuja y fue claramente mejor a este Feyenoord, de nuevo ante su afición. Fue un partido de eficacia, de oficio y experiencia. La que no tienen, salvo excepciones, estos jugadores que Pellegrini ha convertido en un bloque sólido, fiable y que, a sus destellos de sus grandes estrellas, une ahora un espíritu colectivo de los que te suele llevar lejos en este tipo de competiciones. Mandó el Betis desde el inicio. Y hasta el descanso. De principio a fin. Sin goles, sin apenas ocasiones, pero instalados en territorio contrario. De principio a fin. Sin que el Feyenoord, a excepción de una ocasión clarísima en el 43', pudiese amenazar. La erró Zechiël, en un remate a placer que tiró a las nubes. Fue el único nudo que apretó en las miles y miles de gargantas que disfrutaron en La Cartuja de los suyos. La del Betis llegó en un mano a mano que Parrott mandó al cuerpo de Ernst. Mientras el Cucho degustaba canapés en un palco. Cuando el equipo se vaciaba en busca de una opción de gol real. Llegó y como llegó se esfumó. Y con ella el primer tiempo. Los de Pellegrini se iban a vestuarios con el gesto torcido. Sabiendo que en la Champions, cuando tienes tus momentos, hay que aprovecharlos. Buscó el suyo el Feyenoord en la reanudación. Los de Gio Van Bronckhorst tuvieron sus mejores minutos. Siempre con Hadj Moussa como gran amenaza. Muy por encima del resto de su equipo. Y ahí se hicieron gigantes los Bartra, Natan y compañía. Porque este Betis es algo más que las galopadas de Abde, la fantasía de Isco o los regates de Antony. No hay que quedarse solo en la carcasa, hay que ir a ver con detenimiento cada pieza. Cada conexión. Porque todo funciona a las mil maravillas dentro de un engranaje armonioso. Casi perfecto. Y en una de esas manos del fútbol moderno, en la enésima llegada por la izquierda con Fran García y Abde, un centro del marroquí encontró un brazo propicio para poner el balón en el punto de penalti. Y apareció el de las cinco Champions. Para ponerla dentro. Para tirar abajo La Cartuja. Como si se fuese a poner nervioso. A partir de ahí, resistencia. Y resistencia. Y resistencia. Con un equipo comprometido, enchufado y atinado. Que no todo va de correr y ponerle voluntad. También hay que saber. Hasta con un pequeño tinte heroico en ese arreón final del Feyenoord, que pudo empatar de no ser por el nivel defensivo de los de Pellegrini. El Betis es de ese puñado de equipos que, tras tres jornadas, suma nueve puntos. La revelación de esta Champions. Como suena. Y suena muy bien. Tanto como el silbido de las balas de cañón, apiñadas, que plasmó Pepe Alonso en un papel. Ahora Betis, ahora.

articles.title: Courtois les da alas
articles.standfirst: El belga salva en el primer tiempo a un Madrid que llega al Clásico goleando. Bernardo abre la cuenta, Arda brilla, Mbappé hace su gol y Diomande deslumbra en el lugar de un mustio Vini
articles.summary: El belga salva en el primer tiempo a un Madrid que llega al Clásico goleando. Bernardo abre la cuenta, Arda brilla, Mbappé hace su gol y Diomande deslumbra en el lugar de un mustio Vini
articles.body: El Real Madrid completó el pleno de puntos en el arranque de Champions con la contundencia que se le supone. Tramitó el duelo ante el Leipzig con suficiencia, demasiada en el primer acto, hasta invocar la aparición del portero más decisivo del planeta. Salvó dos goles Courtois, imponente, para mantener vivo a su equipo hasta que abriera la lata. Atinó Bernardo, después Arda, el mejor futbolista de campo, y completaron Mbappé y Diomande, que volvió a brillar donde no lo hizo Vinicius. El sorpasso está servido. Al Clásico con una pegada incontestable. En las dos áreas. Por tercer partido consecutivo, Valverde arrancó como capitán y lateral derecho, esta vez en Champions ante el Leipzig. Venían los alemanes de recibir un severo correctivo del Bayern en la Bundes, pero cuando el Madrid juega andando no hay enemigo pequeño. Las rotaciones de Mourinho, con un doble pivote inédito (Camavinga-Bernardo) no agilizaron el juego, y el regreso de Vinicius al verde en plena sanción liguera no resolvió dudas. Puso intención Junior, incluso trabajo en alguna recuperación, pero se ofreció poco. Muy poco. El primer amago de ocasión fue para el departamento de marketing, la contra de la BMV que condujo Bellingham, sirvió Mbappé y no llegó Vinicius al centro-chut del francés. Pero todo lo diferente, lo inesperado, lo desequilibrante, partía casi siempre de pie izquierdo de Arda Güler. Toques de primera, controles, incluso alguna conducción en el área deteniendo el juego, a lo Buitre, de otro nivel Pero como el Madrid no subía el ritmo, el Leipzig se animó y llevó a Courtois a la portada del partido. Primero avisó Nusa con un control estratosférico con desborde a Valverde que no encontró rematador. Después sí apareció Rómulo en el área para volear una pelota sin dueño y obtener el póster de la noche. El de Courtois retorciéndose abajo, a su izquierda, para sacar una pelota imposible para cualquiera salvo para él. Brotaron los primeros silbidos de la hinchada blanca de Champions, que suele ser más bullanguera pero no traga con según qué cosas. Escuchó Mou la silbatina y sacó a sus suplentes a calentar. Espabilen. Respondió casi de inmediato Vinicius al buscar su diagonal favorita, en individual. Le tapó Vandervoort. Es difícil ver combinaciones entre la M y la V. Por lo que sea. Volvió a abusar Nusa de la pasividad en su zona (salvó Rüdiger) y la tuvo Nkunku en un mano a mano. Un coloso naranja le ocultó la portería y dio alas a su equipo. Porque el Madrid te castiga como nadie si perdonas. Bastó un ataque rápido de izquierda a derecha, centro atrás de Valverde, remate de Arda y Bernardo, que ya había aparecido por el área chica en el primer tercio del encuentro, cobró la mala fortuna de Vandervoort en los rebotes. 1-0. Parecía abierto el encuentro al descanso, pero el Leipzig acusó la desventaja más de la cuenta. Valverde empezó a desbordar a la espalda de Güler, que se hinchó a servirle balones. Como el que sacó Vandervoort al minuto. Pero el segundo tanto llegó por el otro lado. Controló Vini en banda, sirvió profundo a Bellingham que templó al segundo palo, cabeceó Mbappé y remachó en la línea Arda. Premio para el crack turco. Partido liquidado. Los cambios de Demichelis buscaron más ahorrar energía para la Bundesliga que buscar el milagro. Quitó primero a Gruda y después a Nusa, sus mejores argumentos ofensivos. Porque a Rómulo Cardoso le cuesta girarse un mundo. Aún así pudo descontar al escaparse de Huijsen en el área y quedarse solo. Apareció por detrás Valverde como una centella para demostrar que es un todocampista único. También sorprendió con sus relevos Mourinho. Quitó a Vinicius, después de una hora larga sin intentar un regate. No tenía que reservarle para el Clásico. Entró Diomande, ex del Leipzig, y también Cucurella, pitado por los cientos de alemanes que había en la grada. Tanto que los madridistas tuvieron que silenciarlos con aplausos al lateral. El modo ahorro de energía antes del Clásico fue evidente en el tramo final, aunque la relajación en las marcas facilitó el tiroteo. Controló solo en la frontal Mbappé y firmó su diana de Champions, al ángulo opuesto. Descontó en la respuesta el Leipzig con un remate cruzado de Gomis, con la zaga blanca descolocada. Y el punto final lo puso Diomande con una volea espectacular a la escuadra. El marfileño, en la izquierda, es demoledor. Como lo fue en su día Vinicius. Saquen sus propias conclusiones.

articles.title: Florida Bar Fires Employee over 'Reprehensible' Comments to Miami Football Player
articles.summary: CORAL GABLES, Fla. (AP) — The Florida Bar has fired an employee after a brief investigation into Instagram direct messages that were sent to a Miami football player after the Hurricanes beat Florida State last weekend.
articles.body:
CORAL GABLES, Fla. (AP) — The Florida Bar has fired an employee after a brief investigation into Instagram direct messages that were sent to a Miami football player after the Hurricanes beat Florida State last weekend.

Kade McLendon, who worked at the Bar for about two years as a computer technician, was fired on Wednesday, the Bar said. An account from a person using McLendon's name sent a number of messages to Miami's Damon Wilson II after the Hurricanes' 43-35 victory , including several racist and homophobic slurs.

Wilson, who is Black, shared a screenshot of the messages publicly Sunday, calling it a "glimpse into the life of a black student athlete." The Bar said Tuesday that McLendon was under investigation.

"Those messages were reprehensible and inconsistent with the mission, values, and policies of The Florida Bar," the group's statement said Wednesday. "While McLendon denies sending the messages, he did not provide evidence sufficient to demonstrate to The Florida Bar's satisfaction that his Instagram account had been compromised. As of today, The Florida Bar has terminated McLendon's employment."

An attempt by The Associated Press to reach McLendon on Tuesday was unsuccessful. It's unclear why the private messages were sent to Wilson, who is in his first season at Miami after previously playing at Georgia and Missouri.

"That's my brother and I embrace him," Miami offensive lineman Ryan Rodriguez said Tuesday when asked about Wilson and the online comments. "It's more than a game. That's my brother."

Miami, the No. 1-ranked team in the AP Top 25 , next plays Saturday at home against Pittsburgh.

articles.title: Manchester United: Bruno Fernandes criticises coaches as Michael Carrick questions players after Champions League loss to Como
articles.summary: Man Utd were thumped 4-1 by Como in the Champions League - a result which left Bruno Fernandes criticising the United coaching staff and Michael Carrick raising the question of motivation and intensity about his players; United are on a seven-game winless run across all competitions
articles.body:
Bruno Fernandes criticised the tactical plan of the Man Utd coaches.

Michael Carrick questioned the motivation of his players.

If only Man Utd's performance on the pitch in Italy was as forceful as the post-match interviews.

As it happened | Teams | Stats | Latest news: Man Utd

After losing at Atletico Madrid last time out in the Champions League, Lisandro Martinez hit out at the club's hierarchy , calling out technical director Jason Wilcox for failings in the transfer window.

This time captain Fernandes took aim at the club's coaching staff in a stinging take-down of their pressing plan.

Asked by TNT Sports about a lack of cohesion in United's work out of possession, Fernandes defended his team-mates and put the blame on Carrick and his coaches.

"It's a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little space in behind and try to get the ball in the first moment, to wait for them, to give them the ball," he said.

"But sometimes when you give too much the ball to these teams they get confident, they have so many bodies behind the ball that make you run a lot, make people get frustrated, and then obviously when you recover the ball the legs are, and the brain, much more difficult to make it work."

Was that tactical idea what cost Man Utd in Como? "That's on the manager and on the staff to see it, it's not on me," said Fernandes.

"I just said, I think sometimes we have to be more brave on the pressure, trying to take a risk of getting that press very high and making them uncomfortable - as they did to us."

A meeting between Carrick, Martinez and Wilcox repaired relations after the centre-back's comments in Madrid. But Carrick gave a blunt response in his post-match press conference on Wednesday when Fernandes' thoughts were put to him.

"We half pressed man-to-man in the second half and ended up conceding a goal from that," he said. "Whatever tactics you play, if you don't run back, you ain't going to win."

'Angry' Carrick: You can't choose when to give absolutely everything

Carrick is usually measured in front of the media but he made his feelings clear after the club's winless run stretched to seven games with this loss.

"I'm really angry," he said. "For us to play in that way is not acceptable."

For all United did wrong in the game, it was the application of his players which was prominent in his post-match assessment.

"I'll definitely look at what we've done [as a coaching staff] or if it's the motivation and the intention and the purpose and the intensity of a game of football you have to bring," he said. "We didn't bring that today.

"You can't turn it on and off and you can't choose when you want to perform or when you don't want to perform or when you give absolutely everything or when you maybe don't," he told TNT Sports.

Carrick, who apologised after the game to United's travelling support, later added in his press conference: "It wasn't just the goals. It was the manner we went about that was the difficult thing to watch. It's not about me right now. The results can come and go, but you've got to do it in a certain way. That wasn't it."

It's now two defeats in three Champions League games this season. Fernandes, Carrick and United will have to show the solutions to their problems at home to Bournemouth on Sunday, live on Sky Sports , if their winless streak is to end in the Premier League this weekend.

articles.title: Declan Rice grabs Arsenal draw at Bayern Munich in Champions League
articles.summary: Eze gave Arsenal the lead, but Davies levelled and Kane netted a penalty for the hosts before Rice made it 2-2.
articles.body:
Declan Rice scored a late equaliser to grab last season’s runners-up Arsenal a 2-2 draw at Bayern Munich in the Champions League.

Eberechi Eze opened the scoring for Arsenal on Wednesday after coming on for the injured Bukayo Saka, but Alphonso Davies brought Bayern level after a sublime pass from Harry Kane.

Kane had Bayern on track for victory when he created and converted a second-half penalty, but his England teammate Rice equalised with eight minutes remaining to earn Arsenal a point.

Bayern were without in-form winger Michael Olise, Germany captain Joshua Kimmich and midfielder Jamal Musiala. Coach Vincent Kompany had been a doubt due to illness but took his place in the dugout.

Despite the absences, Kane ensured Bayern posed a consistent threat against Arsenal’s miserly defence with another excellent performance ahead of next week’s Ballon d’Or ceremony in London.

Kane’s second-half penalty, his 16th goal in 23 matches against Arsenal, extended his scoring streak to 10 straight Champions League games. Kane is one shy of the record held by Cristiano Ronaldo, who scored in 11 consecutive matches for Real Madrid.

The draw was just the second time Arsenal had dropped points in 12 games in all competitions this season.

Arsenal were hit with an early blow when Saka, their joint-top scorer this season, fell to the ground eight minutes in, grabbed his thigh and immediately signalled to the bench.

Bayern’s two previous Champions League opponents this term were from Norway, and the perennial Bundesliga winners seemed to struggle with Arsenal’s physicality as Mikel Arteta’s side pinned them back in the early stages.

With 25 minutes gone, Odegaard floated a simple pass across Bayern’s defence and into the path of the onrushing Eze, who collected and stroked the ball past Manuel Neuer.

Caught out by Eze’s perfectly timed run, the hosts looked even more surprised when VAR overturned the linesman’s offside call and awarded the goal.

The pre-match chatter had been dominated by talk of Kane’s Ballon d’Or prospects, and the England captain showed why he is among the favourites when he set up Davies’s equaliser 10 minutes later.

Kane spotted Davies on the move and threaded the ball through the midfield and around Gabriel for the Canadian winger to guide the ball into the bottom corner.

With the hosts now in the ascendancy, Ezri Konsa saw yellow for taking Kane out of a Bayern counter minutes later.

After the break, Neuer and David Raya took turns producing magnificent saves, with the Bayern captain tipping Bruno Guimaraes’s header onto the crossbar and the Spaniard denying Dayot Upamecano.

Both sides traded surges forward, but Kane would again prove crucial as Bayern took the lead.

Kane’s shot from the edge of the penalty area connected with Jurrien Timber’s arm, with the referee immediately pointing to the spot before Kane stepped up and buried his kick.

Bayern looked to be in control but the match turned again when late substitute Viktor Gyokeres threaded a clever pass to Rice, who slammed in an equaliser.

Kane told TNT Sports he was a little disappointed with the result.

“But probably when you look at the whole 90 minutes, a draw was probably a fair result,” he said.

articles.title: Real Madrid rout RB Leipzig 4-1 to continue perfect Champions League start
articles.summary: Kylian Mbappe and Yan Diomande score stunners as Real beat Leipzig to make it three from three in the Champions League.
articles.body:
Real Madrid claimed a third Champions League victory in as many games, thrashing RB Leipzig 4-1 on Wednesday, with Kylian Mbappe and Yan Diomande among the goalscorers for Jose Mourinho’s side.

Bernardo Silva opened the scoring for Madrid from close range late in a tight first half, with Arda Guler doubling the advantage of the record 15-time European champions soon after the interval.

Mbappe bent home a third before Tidiam Gomis pulled one back for the German side, and Diomande rammed a volley into the top corner late on to cap Madrid’s triumph.

Their fourth consecutive win across all competitions will boost Madrid’s morale ahead of Sunday’s La Liga Clasico against bitter rivals Barcelona.

Without a major trophy in two seasons and after a shaky domestic start, Madrid can at least boast a perfect record in Europe, unlike Barca after their defeat at Paris Saint-Germain on Tuesday.

Mourinho started Vinicius, serving a four-match ban in La Liga, on the left flank and benched former Leipzig winger Diomande, despite his improving form.

The coach also brought Bernardo Silva and Eduardo Camavinga into midfield and put midfielder Federico Valverde at right-back again, as he did in Sunday’s win at Sevilla.

Visitors Leipzig created the first big chance, with Madrid stopper Thibaut Courtois getting down low to make a superb save from Romulo Cardoso.

Vinicius, who improved on a poor showing at Roma last week without breaking out of his rut, drew a full-stretch save from Leipzig’s Maarten Vandevoordt.

Madrid carved out an advantage in the final stages of a low-key first half when Valverde cut the ball back for Guler, whose shot Vandevoordt saved. However, the goalkeeper could not clear it, and Silva darted in to prod over the line.

It was the former Manchester City midfielder’s first goal for the club after joining this summer.

Vandevoordt saved well from Valverde’s fierce effort before Guler put Madrid two goals ahead in the 52nd minute.

Jude Bellingham crossed to the back post and Mbappe nodded the ball across goal, with Guler able to hold off a defender and turn home.

Mbappe lashed a shot into the side netting after Bellingham teed it up, as Madrid looked to put the game out of sight.

Mourinho sent on Diomande for Vinicius with 20 minutes remaining, and the Brazilian looked disappointed on the bench, knowing he cannot play again until November 4, when Madrid visit AEK Athens.

Madrid’s record 140 million-euro ($157m) signing, Diomande, pulled the ball back to Mbappe on the edge of the box for Madrid’s third, and the French forward bent it home.

Leipzig quickly grabbed a consolation goal at the other end as Dean Huijsen switched off, with Gomis firing past Courtois.

Diomande ended proceedings with a bang, rattling an emphatic volley from Brahim Diaz’s cross into the top corner for his third goal in his last four appearances.

articles.summary: El extremo está feliz y repleto de confianza
articles.body: Voy a intentarlo, un toque y boom". Así explicó Diomande su golazo ante el Leipzig, con una gran sonrisa, con la mochila en la espalda ya con menos peso que en el mes de agosto. Está feliz el delantero de Costa de Marfil, que se atreve con todo, que le sale todo: "No es fácil, claro que no es fácil... parece fácil decirlo pero no hacerlo. Diomande ya lleva tres goles en el Real Madrid, los tres en el Santiago Bernabéu casi de manera consecutiva: ante Villarreal, Sevilla y Leipzig. articles.title: Man United captain Fernandes slams Carrick’s tactics after Como hammering
articles.summary: Manchester United winless run continues with 4-1 Champions League humbling in Como, and Bruno Fernandes slams tactics.
articles.body:
Manchester United captain Bruno ‌Fernandes said his side failed to apply enough pressure and adopted ⁠a “mood of defeat” ⁠after conceding early in Wednesday’s 4–1 Champions League loss at Como, a result that increased scrutiny on manager Michael Carrick.

Como opened the scoring ⁠in the second minute, and United collapsed, with only a stoppage-time consolation goal from Joshua Zirkzee making the scoreline slightly less severe.

“We started on the wrong ⁠foot, and they scored very early,” Fernandes told TNT Sports. “There was not enough pressure on the ball and not many good movements off the ball. There were many things not going our way.

“It’s a decision from the [coaching] staff not to press man-to-man ‌and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said.

Asked if his comments amounted to criticism of Carrick’s tactics, Fernandes said: “That’s on the manager and staff to see, not me.

“Sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of pressing high and ⁠making them uncomfortable.”

Carrick has come under increasing pressure with ⁠United now winless in seven matches.

“It was more than disappointing,” the 45-year-old manager told TNT Sports. “I think everybody’s got to take responsibility for that. I’ll take responsibility for the overall team and performance; it stops with me, and I’m fine with that.

“But as a supporter of this football club, to see a ⁠performance like that is unacceptable, I have to ⁠say.”

Carrick said his side had failed to show the required intensity.

“It’s the motivation and the purpose and the intensity of a game of football that you have to bring. We didn’t bring that today,” ‌he said. “I’ve got to apologise for the performance.”

Fernandes also questioned United’s mentality after the early setback.

“Conceding early makes us go into the game with a mood ‌of ‌defeat,” he said.

United have three points from their opening three Champions League matches and host AS Roma in their next fixture in the competition.

articles.title: Aston Villa 3-1 Viking: Alysson stars as Unai Emery’s side make it three wins from three in the Champions League
articles.summary: Match report as Aston Villa made it three wins from three in this season’s Champions League with a 3-1 win over Norwegian champions Viking at Villa Park. Ross Barkley and Emiliano Buendia scored in the first half. Only a late Viking goal denied Villa top spot
articles.body:
Ross Barkley headed Unai Emery's side in front midway through the first half and Emiliano Buendia's penalty made it two before the break. Alysson's run led to an own goal for the third with only Peter Christiansen's late volley taking Villa off top spot.

Bayern Munich struggled against the Norwegian champions last week but Villa were in control from the start despite a makeshift look to the side with Joao Gomes at right-back. The Brazilian had a cross deflected against the underside of the bar early in the game.

Ibrahim Mbaye's corner from the other flank was nodded in by Barkley soon after before Buendia came close with two good headed chances. The Argentine made amends from the penalty spot when a VAR check ruled that Alysson had been clipped inside the box.

The young winger was the best player on the pitch, producing surely his best performance in a Villa shirt. He was instrumental in the third goal too, racing through from deep. Henrik Heggheim could only divert his cross past his own goalkeeper.

That was the goal that took Villa into top spot in this league phase. The crowd knew it too, chanting 'We are top of the league' afterwards. But Peter Christiansen's brilliant late volley - awarded after a VAR check - dropped them back to second behind PSG.

The tifo unveiled in the Holte End before kick-off pointed out that Villa have conquered before and are prepared for more. There are more fancied sides in this Champions League but few boast the clarity of purpose that Emery brings. Villa are building again.

Aston Villa are the second quickest team to record 20 wins in the European Cup (30 matches), behind only Real Madrid (29 matches).

Villa have won each of their last 12 major European home games, the joint-longest run by an English team this century.

Villa are the first Europa League holders to win their first three games of a Champions League campaign since Manchester United in 2017.

Emiliano Buendia speaking about Alysson to TNT Sports:

"He was incredible. He's showing his potential, his ability on the wing. Also Ibrahim Mbaye as well - their speed, their qualities. It's going to help the team a lot, so it's very important to have them and to try to help them to improve because they are young talents."

Aston Villa manager Unai Emery speaking in the press conference:

"We are delighted how we are responding in our demands, respecting the competition of the Champions League and respecting the opponent, and how we are improving things. Through those issues I think we played a good match, collectively, tactically, respecting them, following the plan we set on.

"Then, individually, the players showed their qualities. I think we did a good job and some players did a step forward in their confidence, feeling better, understanding everything tactically and playing their football."

Emery likely had his wingers in mind. When asked about Mbaye and Alysson, he replied: "It was a step forward for both players in our idea, so really happy." There was praise too for Alejandro Garnacho who "played his best minutes" in a late cameo off the bench.

Viking head coach Morten Jensen speaking in the press conference:

"The second half was much more like Viking wants to be. Maybe we had too much respect in the first half, they were all over us and we did not create much offensively, which is rare for Viking.

"I think we did a much better job by asking questions of Villa's midfield and their defence and ended up drawing the second half. That is something that we can build on for the future.

"It is the next level for us as a team and really great to see the team get a goal at Villa Park in front of over 2,000 Norwegian fans."

articles.title: Bayern Munich 2-2 Arsenal: Declan Rice secures draw for Gunners in Champions League after Harry Kane penalty
articles.summary: Match report as Declan Rice cancels out Harry Kane's penalty to rescue a 2-2 draw for Arsenal against Bayern Munich at the Allianz Arena; Eberechi Eze scored the opener after replacing the injured Bukayo Saka but Alphonso Davies levelled
articles.body:
Arsenal were heading for a first defeat in 14 league phase or group stage games before a slick passing move involving Noni Madueke and Viktor Gyokeres allowed Rice to race into the box and fire a clinical finish beyond Manuel Neuer from an acute angle.

Earlier, Eberechi Eze had scored the opener in similar style from a Martin Odegaard pass after replacing Bukayo Saka, who was forced off with an injury Mikel Arteta later said "doesn't look good at all", but Harry Kane inspired Bayern's recovery.

The former Spurs striker, who is one of the leading contenders to win the Ballon d'Or at Monday's ceremony, set up Alphonso Davies' leveller with a superb through-ball before converting their second goal from the spot after Jurrien Timber had handled.

Kane's goal was his 16th in 22 appearances against Arsenal and made him only the second player after Cristiano Ronaldo to score in 10 consecutive Champions League games.

Bayern were missing Michael Olise due to suspension and Joshua Kimmich due to a death in his family but still created numerous chances, with David Raya brilliantly saving the best of them when he clawed away a close-range header from Davies.

But Arsenal were a threat too, despite Saka's withdrawal. Bayern needed a superb piece of goalkeeping from Manuel Neuer to prevent a Bruno Guimaraes header from crossing the line after half-time.

Kane's penalty, after his shot had struck Timber's arm, arrived not long afterwards, but it was his England team-mate Rice who ended up having the final say on a dramatic night.

Analysis: Arsenal display defies style critics

Arsenal faced criticism of their playing style after their 1-0 win over Nottingham Forest. Their performance against Bayern Munich, at one of the toughest grounds in Europe, was a suitable riposte.

Many expected Mikel Arteta's side to sit back and try to frustrate Bayern, who hadn't lost in 39 home league phase or group stage games. Instead, they went blow for blow with them.

They allowed the hosts more chances than Mikel Arteta might have liked. But they created plenty too, showing attacking intent from the early stages of the game right until the end, when their perseverance was rewarded by Rice's superbly-worked equaliser.

Arsenal finished the game having had more shots and more possession than Bayern in their own back yard. They might have had a win to show for their efforts, too, if not for some Neuer heroics.

Saka's injury, confirmed as a quad issue as he attempted to play a pass, was a blot on the night for Arsenal. Arteta admitted the club's medical staff are worried about it in his post-match interview and was similarly pessimistic in his press conference.

"They are a bit concerned," the Arsenal manager said to TNT Sports . "A player that has to come off with a really sharp pain is never good news, but we have to wait and see."

"Those things happen unfortunately," he added in his press conference. "It doesn't look good at all but we have to wait and see."

The Gunners are already without Christos Tzolis due to injury, meaning the only wide option other than Eze on the bench against Bayern Munich was the 16-year-old Max Dowman.

Saturday's meeting with Everton begins a busy run of five games before the November international break, including a trip to Anfield to face Liverpool in the Premier League on November 1. It remains to be seen whether Saka will be available to feature.

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta to TNT Sports : "What a game. That's one of the highest levels that we have played, the level of the opposition, what the game required, and our level as well.

"Two teams that wanted to press each other constantly. Two teams that wanted to attack and play. I think it was a fascinating game.

"I think we started the game incredibly well. We were so dominant. We did everything to deserve the first goal. We didn't score it, then we lost Bukayo, who was having a great game.

"We had to adapt to it. We gave a chance away after our corner that could have cost us a goal, then they scored a goal. And then in the second half, the game was very even. They scored the second goal and then you have to react, and we certainly did, with the spirit of the team and the quality of the goal as well.

"It's remarkable what we've done. I watched all the games they've played here in the last three years and they batter every team with many goals. So I really value and I'm really aware that what the boys have done tonight is special."

Kane: I always get penalties against Arsenal

Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane to TNT Sports : "A little bit of disappointment, but I think a draw was a fair result.

"We looked like the team that was going to go on and win it. They then put us under a bit of pressure and got the goal.

"We can't be too disappointed. We take the point and move on."

On his penalty: "I wouldn't say never in doubt! A lot of practice and hard work goes into penalties. It was nice to get on the scoresheet. I always seem to get penalties against Arsenal!"

articles.title: El enfado de Antony tras el cambio
articles.standfirst: "Se marchó al vestuario un minuto y volvió. No hubo ningún problema con eso", dijo Pellegrini, que le restó importancia
articles.summary: "Se marchó al vestuario un minuto y volvió. No hubo ningún problema con eso", dijo Pellegrini, que le restó importancia
articles.body: Nueve de nueve en la Fase Liga de la Champions. El Betis ha ganado sus tres partidos en el máximo torneo continental, como Real Madrid, PSG, Liverpool y Aston Villa. Está entre los cinco elegidos. El partido frente al Feyenoord dejó un nuevo recital de Isco, que rubricó el triunfo con un gol de penalti en el segundo tiempo, pero no todo fueron sonrisas, porque Antony se marchó enfadado tras ser sustituido en la segunda parte. No tuvo su día el brasileño, que no fue el jugador desequilibrante de otros partidos. No pudo explotar su velocidad y desborde por el costado y se marchó frustrado del terreno de juego cuando Pellegrini le sustituyó en el minuto 64. Según captaron las cámaras de Movistar, Antony lanzó al suelo la sudadera cuando se dirigía al vestuario. Pellegrini restó importancia al enfado del brasileño. "El cambio es por decisión técnica. Estábamos perdiendo el balón, había jugadores que también eran alternativas. Antony se marchó al vestuario un minuto y volvió. No hubo ningún problema con eso", afirmó el entrenador del Betis.

articles.standfirst: Al otro lado del espejo
articles.summary: Al otro lado del espejo
articles.body: El Madrid no termina de sujetar los partidos, pero tiene un portero especial y es muy resolutivo arriba. Vista la alineación de anoche, parece que Mourinho insiste en la nueva línea, pues formó la media de nuevo con mezcla de músculo y mando, en este caso Camavinga y Bernardo Silva, y Valverde en la derecha, con la banda para él. Lo pasó mal atrás ante el noruego Nusa, un extremo excelente, pero por arriba dio mucho. Güler, partiendo de extremo derecho, estuvo de nuevo estupendo e hizo todo lo mejor del Madrid en la primera media hora mientras el equipo terminaba de encajarse. Y ya llegamos a Vinicius, que asomó en esta oportunidad europea y estuvo sólo regular para lo que es él. Se apuntó dos buenas diagonales con remate final, sacándole las dos mejores paradas al portero, pero eso fue todo. No intentó ni un regate. Posiblemente nota que no tiene aquella velocidad que le conocíamos y prefiere no arriesgar. Se retiró triste, con la cara del que sabe que necesita hacer más. Cuando al final salió Diomande para soltarse con vistas al Clásico hizo bastante más en el poco rato que le correspondió. Suyo fue el pase que Mbappé convirtió en el 3-1 y suyo fue el 4-1, una volea tremenda. El resultado es lucido, una goleada siempre sienta bien, y permitió sacar la cabeza a Bernardo Silva, que hasta marcó. La curiosidad ahora es si Mourinho persistirá en el Camp Nou con este modelo, el 4-2-3-1 con mezcla de músculo y batuta en el doble pivote o si apostará más por dificultar el juego del Barça en esa zona. Recordemos que en su primera época solía enviar a Pepe al mediocampo para protegerse. Ya veremos. De lo que no hay duda, aunque sea penoso aceptarlo, es que la suspensión de Vinicius le viene mal a él, pero no al Madrid. Diomande está ahora mismo en posición de hacer mucho más, tanto que hace dudar sobre cuál será el futuro de esa posición. Pero todo eso ya llegará. De momento, el Madrid tiene 9 puntos de 9 en la Champions, y lo mismo ese EuroBetis que planta firme.

articles.title: Bukayo Saka's injury 'does not look good at all' - Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta
articles.summary: Mikel Arteta says the quadriceps injury Arsenal's Bukayo Saka picked up in the Champions League draw with Bayern Munich "does not look good at all".
articles.body:
Mikel Arteta says the quadriceps injury Arsenal 's Bukayo Saka picked up in the 2-2 Champions League draw against Bayern Munich "does not look good at all".

The 25-year-old winger went down in the 10th minute at Allianz Arena - attempting to play a pass with nobody around him - and had to be replaced by Eberechi Eze, who went on to score the opening goal.

"They are a bit concerned. A player who has to come off with a really sharp pain is never good news but we have to wait and see," Arteta told TNT Sports.

Saka has had fitness issues in recent months and his game time was managed at the end of last season, as well as with England at the World Cup, because of an Achilles injury he picked up in March.

He missed the March international break and seven games for the Gunners, but returned to help them lift the Premier League title for the first time in 22 years.

Saka started the Champions League final defeat by Paris St-Germain but was substituted after 54 minutes, and only started three of England's eight games at the World Cup - scoring a hat-trick in the 6-4 third-place win over France.

The forward also had surgery on a hamstring injury he picked up in December 2024, which kept him out for 101 days in the 2024-25 season.

He made 49 appearances as Arsenal won the title last term, despite a stop-start season - as well as the Achilles issue, he pulled out of the warm-up against Leeds with a hip injury in January and a hamstring problem kept him out for about four weeks.

But he remains vital to the Gunners, whose win percentage is notably more impressive with him in the team.

Rice scores late as Arsenal draw with Bayern

Despite the loss of Saka early on in the game, Arsenal still produced a good performance and could have won the match late on after Declan Rice's late equaliser.

"The only negative is seeing one of their star players, Saka, having to pull up with an injury early in the first half," said Champions League Match of the Day pundit Nedum Onuoha.

"He was lying on the floor with his hand up and he knew he was in a bit of trouble, so now the concern will be how long he is out for.

"It's not necessarily something that means the team will struggle heavily, but there is a reason why he is regarded as one of the best players in this Arsenal team and is seen as being important for them."

After Saka's withdrawal Noni Madueke, who had started on the left wing, switched to the right and looked bright, while Eze scored the opening goal from the left after coming off the bench.

"This is one of the reasons their squad has been built the way it has been and I think Madueke and Eze did well on the wings today after Saka came off," added Onuoha.

"In terms of options, at this moment in time for Arsenal , it is not going to be an issue - they will miss the star power that he has, they still have plenty of other wide players who can step up and do the job while they wait for him to come back."

Arsenal 's style of play has been criticised this season but, even before Saka's withdrawal, the Gunners played on the front foot and enjoyed more possession than their German opponents.

Losing Saka, who has scored four goals in 11 appearances in all competitions, will be tough to deal with.

But the Gunners have invested heavily in their squad over the past two summer transfer windows and have options.

Madueke can play on both wings, while summer signing Christos Tzolis - although currently out with a hamstring injury - has started the season well.

The Gunners also have 16-year-old Max Dowman as an attacking option, and the youngster has already shown that he can have an impact for the senior side after scoring in the Premier League last season.

Arteta, who was asked what the rest of the forward line will need to do in Saka's absence, said he was pleased with what he saw against Bayern.

"I think Ebs [Eze] had a great game. Not only the ball, but the actions. His overall performance, I think his commitment without the ball as well," he said.

"And when the other ones come in, I think they really contributed to this. First of all, the energy.

"And then to bring different tools that the team needed in that moment to get something out of the game. So, very pleased again."

articles.title: Bayern Munich: 'Ridiculous' Harry Kane underlines Ballon d'Or credentials
articles.summary: Why Declan Rice backs his England team-mate Harry Kane to win the Ballon d'Or after Arsenal's draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League.
articles.body:
Even by Harry Kane's remarkable standards, this was mightily impressive.

There were fewer than 25 minutes on the clock during Bayern Munich's thrilling 2-2 draw with Arsenal in the Champions League when the forward took matters into his own hands in a bid to break the deadlock.

As the Premier League champions prepared to defend a Bayern goal-kick, Kane seized the initiative by launching his side up the pitch with a raking 80-yard pass.

It was a moment of remarkable ingenuity from the England international, one that almost ended with Bayern taking the lead.

"Under Vincent Kompany, he has been given a level of trust that he has probably never had before under any other manager," former Manchester City defender Nedum Onuoha told BBC Sport.

"For all the things we've seen him do and the positions we've seen him roam into, nobody has seen him take a goal-kick before.

"But even someone like Manuel Neuer, who is his senior and has been at Bayern for a large part of his career, sees Harry Kane put the ball down and thinks, 'OK, sure'. He lets Harry go for it because he thinks whatever he sees is going to be correct.

"At the same time, there were Bayern players running forward because they knew that the ball could come.

"For him to be taking a goal-kick is not something you may want to see very often. You don't necessarily want your number nine to be THAT deep, but the nature of his game when he is playing for Bayern is to roam, and today it was a huge benefit to the team."

Although Kane was denied the opportunity to add another outstanding assist to his already impressive catalogue, he did not have to wait long to make another decisive contribution.

After Eberechi Eze had put Arsenal ahead, Kane helped Bayern restore parity, bending a sumptuous pass around Jurrien Timber for Alphonso Davies to finish.

The England captain then fired the hosts in front from the penalty spot midway through the second half, taking his career tally of goals against Arsenal to 16.

But Declan Rice struck late on to earn Arsenal a share of the spoils.

'When you play against him, you see how much of a pain it is'

For Kane, it was another mesmerising performance that underlined his credentials as the frontrunner for the 2026 Ballon d'Or.

The former Tottenham Hotspur captain, 33, could become the first Englishman since Michael Owen in 2001 to win the prestigious individual award, with Barcelona's Lamine Yamal and Paris St-Germain forward and current holder Ousmane Dembele among the favourites.

Kane was named on the 30-man shortlist in September, with the winner due to be announced on Monday following a vote by an international jury of 100 journalists.

"He is the clear winner. His numbers speak for themselves. The year he has had has been remarkable," Arsenal and England midfielder Declan Rice told TNT Sports.

"When you play with him, you realise how good he is, and when you play against him, you see how much of a pain it is.

"He is ridiculous, such a good player, and I am lucky I can play with him, not so lucky I have to play against him."

By scoring against Arsenal on Wednesday night, Kane became only the second player in Champions League history to find the net in 10 consecutive matches.

The only other player to achieve the feat was five-time Ballon d'Or winner Cristiano Ronaldo, who scored in 11 successive matches for Real Madrid between June 2017 and April 2018.

"Kane certainly looks at home at Bayern. He understands the team and its system, and they all understand him. They know that when he gets the ball at his feet, wherever that may be, something good can happen," Onuoha added.

"I think all the Bayern players are really playing into that, but then Harry steps up and scores a penalty as well.

"Having freedom is probably the best way to describe what he has got playing for Bayern, because he will work hard defensively, which allows him the freedom to be creative when he is in attack. For now, he certainly is thriving."

Kane's goal against Arsenal took his tally to 156 in 158 appearances since joining Bayern Munich from Tottenham in 2023.

It was another night to remember for the England captain, but the best could yet be to come, with the Ballon d'Or ceremony in London looming.

"It would be amazing to win," said Kane afterwards. "The voting closed a long time ago so there's nothing I can do, just wait and see what happens."
